notes: Exotic-capable ER with a call-ahead caveat.

q: How do I report animal abuse?
notes: Reporting cruelty goes to the police, not to animal care. The word 'animal' trips the wildlife vocabulary, so this used to answer with a wild bird hospital.

q: my neighbor is beating his dog what do I do
notes: A bystander reporting cruelty. Must not be answered with a dog rescue.

q: I think there is a dogfighting ring near me
notes: Organised fighting: HSUS tip line, or 911 if it is in progress.

q: someone on my block keeps their dog chained outside with no shelter
notes: Ongoing neglect, the classic 311 case rather than 911.

q: how do I save a dog on the at risk list
notes: The at-risk list is time-limited; the answer must explain that only a New Hope partner can pull the animal.

q: I want to rescue a dog before it is put down
notes: Plain wording for the same thing. Nobody searches for the programme by name.

q: what is new hope
notes: The jargon should still resolve, for anyone who has been told the name.

q: how do I pull a dog from the shelter
notes: 'Pull' is the term rescues use; members of the public pick it up from ACC's own pages.

q: found a baby wild rabbit in my yard in queens, the nest got dug up
notes: Wild cottontails need a licensed rehabber, not a domestic-rabbit rescue. Cottontail Cottage is the referral NYC rabbit groups give; it was missing from the site until 2026-09-22.

q: my elderly cat needs a new home, I am on the upper east side and can no longer care for her
notes: Frankie's Feline Fund takes senior-cat surrenders in Manhattan. Its name collides with Frankie's Friends, a vet-bill fund, so a search for it used to find the wrong one.

q: my dog is bleeding badly, is there an emergency vet open now on staten island
notes: Staten Island has two 24/7 hospitals. Until 2026-11-03 one was listed under the wrong name and VEG New Dorp was missing.

q: my cat is having trouble breathing, I'm in chelsea, where is an emergency vet open 24 hours
notes: VEG Chelsea is the 24/7 hospital in the neighbourhood; it was missing until 2026-11-03.

q: my dog cut his paw badly and it won't stop bleeding, we're in park slope
notes: Park Slope has a daytime practice that takes emergencies (Animal Kind). It is listed, but the question gives no time, so a 24/7 hospital must come first.

q: my cat ate a hair tie and is vomiting, upper east side, where can I take her
notes: The Upper East Side has daytime urgent care (URvet, One Love) and 24/7 hospitals (AMC, VEG); the 24/7 ones come first.

q: there is a pregnant stray cat in my building in queens, who can help
notes: Makin' Biscuits' own form offers support with a pregnant cat; 'pregnant' reached no tag until 2026-11-04.

q: my elderly cat needs somewhere to go, I'm in manhattan
notes: Frankie's Feline Fund describes itself as for elderly cats; 'elderly' was not read as senior until 2026-11-04.

q: I'm about to lose my apartment and go into a shelter, what happens to my cat
notes: City shelters do not take pets; the guide covers emotional support animal requests, intake addresses (two moved in August 2026) and boarding.

q: can I bring my emotional support animal into a homeless shelter in nyc
notes: A Reasonable Accommodation Request is needed, and the animal cannot stay while it is reviewed.

q: my dog is bleeding and won't stop, where do I go
notes: 11pm in Park Slope: the nearest places open now are VERG (0.7 mi) and BluePearl Brooklyn (0.9 mi). Animal Kind is nearer but closed.

q: my dog is bleeding and won't stop, where do I go
notes: 3pm: Animal Kind (0.2 mi) is open until 7pm and takes emergencies; so are the two 24/7 hospitals under a mile away.

notes: New Dorp at night: the Staten Island 24/7 hospitals, not Manhattan ones.
